jupas.shortDescription: an class="before_label">Short Description The Department of Japanese Studies provides academic and professional training in the study of Japan and the Japanese language. The programme is designed to meet the growing demand for globally aware citizens, promote cultural and academic exchange, and facilitate communication and cooperation between Hong Kong and Japan. The programme provides training in critical approaches to Japanese society and culture, and is geared towards mastery of the Japanese language. All third-year students are required to spend one academic year in Japan and take unit-bearing courses at a Japanese exchange partner university. A key theme of the programme is a field research project. Second-year students are trained in research methodologies that they then implement in their third year of study in Japan, when they conduct research in the field. In the fourth year of study, students use the material collected during their field research to write an academic research paper. The programme offers three optional streams: (1) Business and Management; (2) Japan in Global Perspective; and (3) Japanese Language and Linguistics. Each stream provides specialised training in the named area and allows students to take courses from other relevant departments, including the Departments of Management, Sociology, Anthropology and Linguistics and Modern Languages. Students who select one of these streams must choose a relevant topic for their final-year project.

cuhkAdmission.introduction: Realize your exchange dream in Japan and Foster Your Cultural Sensitivity, Global Awareness and Intercultural Communication! The major programme in Japanese Studies is an intensive and rigorous undergraduate programme that includes both culture and society courses, as well as language courses at various levels. We provide a wide range of courses to meet student needs, including Japanese culture, history, pop-culture, literature, management and philosophy. In Years 1 and 2, students in the major programme take core courses in Japanese culture and society, Japanese language, and field-research methods, and students begin to formulate ideas for their final-year project (FYP). Year 3 is spent in Japan studying as an exchange student at one of our 21 partner universities in Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka, Kyoto, Hokkaido and Kyushu, while also conducting original research for their final-year project. In Year 4, the students return to CUHK to write their final-year project/thesis, and take elective courses in Japanese studies, along with other courses required by the University. We also offer a Double Major Programme in Japanese Studies and History, which students can complete in four years. The Department also provides opportunities for local and overseas summer internship programmes, and short-term summer exchange programmes. Various scholarships are available from the University and Department for students taking our major. Our programme thus immerses students in a cross-cultural experience through our unique course offerings and study-abroad opportunities, and cultivates cultural sensitivity, global awareness and intercultural communication.

campus.title: Campus Life
content: CUHK's main campus is located in Shatin, offering a spacious and scenic environment with modern facilities.
The University has a unique college system, providing students with a close-knit community and holistic education.
The Department of Japanese Studies offers local and overseas summer internship programmes, as well as short-term summer exchange programmes.
Students benefit from exchange opportunities with 21 partner universities in Japan, including prestigious institutions in Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka, Kyoto, Hokkaido and Kyushu.
Various scholarships are available from the University and Department for students taking the major.

tips.title: Ace Sir's JUPAS Strategy — 9 Actionable Tips
content: - The median admission score for 2025 was 24.5 (Best 5). Aim for at least this to be competitive.
- The lower quartile was 23, so scores below this are unlikely to secure an offer.
- Although not a formal requirement, strong Japanese language skills (e.g., N3 or above) can be an advantage.
- Consider taking the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT) to demonstrate proficiency.
- The programme requires an interview. Prepare to discuss your interest in Japan, your academic goals, and your motivation for studying Japanese Studies.
- Be ready to talk about your understanding of Japanese culture, society, and current affairs.
- The programme accepts any 2 elective subjects at Level 3. Choose subjects that align with your interests and strengths.
- Subjects like History, Geography, or a language can be particularly relevant.
- The programme values cultural sensitivity and global awareness. Showcase any international experiences, exchange programmes, or cross-cultural activities in your application.
**6. Prepare for the Year in Japan**
- All third-year students spend a year in Japan. Demonstrate your adaptability and willingness to immerse yourself in a new environment.
- Research the partner universities and consider which location suits your interests.
- Focus on achieving high grades in your core subjects, especially Chinese and English, as they are weighted in the admission score.
- Mathematics and electives also contribute to the Best 5 calculation.
- Familiarise yourself with the three streams: Business and Management, Japan in Global Perspective, and Japanese Language and Linguistics.
- Tailor your personal statement to reflect your interest in a specific stream.
- Ensure you meet all general entrance requirements, including the specific Applied Learning course acceptance policy.
- Submit your JUPAS application by the deadline and monitor your Band A status.

curriculum.title: 課程結構
content: 日本研究課程是一個密集且嚴謹的本科課程，涵蓋文化與社會課程，以及各級別的語言課程。
第一及第二年：學生修讀日本文化與社會、日語及實地研究方法的必修課程，並開始構思畢業專題項目（FYP）。
第三年：所有學生須在日本其中一所夥伴大學（共 21 所，位於東京、名古屋、大阪、京都、北海道及九州）進行為期一學年的交流，同時為畢業專題進行原創研究。
第四年：學生返回中大撰寫畢業專題/論文，並選修日本研究選修課程及其他大學規定課程。
課程提供三個選修分流：
每個分流提供專門訓練，並允許學生修讀其他相關學系的課程，包括管理學、社會學、人類學及語言學及現代語言系。
另設有日本研究與歷史雙主修課程，學生可在四年內完成。

career.title: 就業前景
content: 畢業生具備良好的英語及日語能力，以及批判性思維和分析技巧。
學生在畢業前參加日本語能力試驗（N1），合格率達 90%，本地及全球院校中無可比擬。
畢業生適合多種就業領域：
部分畢業生繼續深造，取得法律、人類學、新聞學、社會工作等領域的研究生學位。
僱主包括：香港特區政府、滙豐銀行、醫院管理局、三井銀行、道瓊斯、北海道大學及早稻田大學。

日本研究學系提供本地及海外暑期實習計劃，以及短期暑期交流計劃。
學生可透過與日本 21 所夥伴大學（包括東京、名古屋、大阪、京都、北海道及九州）的交流機會獲益。
大學及學系為日本研究主修學生提供多項獎學金。

tips.title: Ace Sir 的 JUPAS 策略 — 9 個實用貼士
content: **1. 目標分數：24.5（中位數）或以上**
- 2025 年中位入學分數為 24.5（最佳 5 科）。力爭達到此分數以增加競爭力。
- 下四分位數為 23，低於此分數獲取錄機會較低。
- 雖然非正式要求，但良好的日語能力（如 N3 或以上）可成為優勢。
- 考慮參加日本語能力試驗（JLPT）以證明能力。
- 課程需要面試。準備討論你對日本的興趣、學術目標及修讀日本研究的動機。
- 準備談論你對日本文化、社會及時事的了解。
- 課程接受任何 2 個選修科目達第 3 級。選擇與你興趣及優勢相符的科目。
- 歷史、地理或語言等科目尤其相關。
- 課程重視文化敏感度及全球意識。在申請中展示任何國際經驗、交流計劃或跨文化活動。
**6. 為日本交流年做好準備**
- 所有三年級學生須在日本度過一年。展示你的適應能力及融入新環境的意願。
- 研究夥伴大學，考慮哪個地點符合你的興趣。
- 專注於核心科目（尤其中文及英文）取得高分，因為它們會計入入學分數。
- 數學及選修科亦影響最佳 5 科計算。
- 熟悉三個分流：商業與管理、全球視野下的日本、日語與語言學。
- 在個人陳述中反映你對特定分流的興趣。
- 確保符合所有一般入學要求，包括特定應用學習課程的接納政策。
- 在截止日期前提交 JUPAS 申請，並監察你的 Band A 狀態。
